method: For each of four query rounds, one unique cold pointed query per tenant (128 distinct tenants) used a unique field to avoid query-result-cache hits. Each layout ran one graph then one graph per tenant at an independently bounded offered concurrency. No application retries. All graph reads verified exact answer and snapshotSeq >= 1; max in-flight was measured in the driver. The single-graph case issued 128 requests into one GraphCoordinatorDO; tenant mode issued one request per each of 128 graph authorities.
interpretation: This single local sample had 100% exact completion and p99 under 100 ms at concurrency 16, 32 and 64 in both layouts. At concurrency 128, both layouts missed the p99 target by 40–46 ms; tenant partitioning was slightly slower in this phase. It does not certify reliability, externally observed latency, a hosted capacity envelope or unbounded scaling.
limitations: One closed-loop Miniflare/SQLite sample on one machine; caller timing is inside the local Worker RPC harness, not network-to-Cloudflare caller latency.
No repeated trials, open-loop arrival-rate test, mixed read/write traffic, failure injection, multi-region or hosted placement.
The experiment partitions 128 independent tenants; it does not test 128 concurrent reads for a single hot tenant. Tenant graph IDs have separate transaction histories and no cross-graph snapshot.
The shared layout commits all 512 seed facts in one graph transaction; the per-tenant layout commits four facts in each of 128 transactions. It is not a write-cost comparison.
